Read: The only authoritative state for the ETS 6.3/6.4 naming pass. It is deliberately short. History lives in git; long-form notes live in archive/ and are not read during normal work.

Inventories.Methods: D:\knx_analysis\perf-now\review63-<module>.json (raw --review; this is the only inventory that also lists imethod_N rows)

Backlog.Note: Measured from the tool's own inventories at v370. The previous 536 counted only part of the method worklist and no types or fields; 12,019 of the 15,742 named rows are SDK-protected coverage the whitelist already covers.
Routes: operation-name literal (perf-now/propose-from-literals.py): a row passes its own name to the logger
contract family: one virtual/interface row names its whole family; the wave expands it
structural fallback: offsets, bitfields, formatters, tables (slow; last)

NextItemRules: Oracle rows are the strongest route: the 6.4 released surface names them, and a literal in the 6.3 body must corroborate the row before it is accepted.
A NewName may not repeat inside one type; the sibling stays open rather than taking a numeric suffix.

Virtual rows, interface implementations and contract-family members are renamed as a family (build-rows.py fills ContractFamily; the updater expands it), so a block can grow the map by more rows than the review file holds.
One block is one review file, one --wave run, one checkpoint, one commit.

Codes: same-module name collision where the sibling has no distinct evidence
HardBlockers.Rule: A turn may stop with work left only when every remaining row of the current block carries one of these codes, recorded here with its token. 'Evidence is missing' is not a blocker code; the turn must switch route instead.
